# 65 · “Even sadder”: “Low Marks Again” as a staged video

*The picture is not reproduced here: it is an edit of a painting by Fyodor Reshetnikov (1952), which is not in the public domain. It is described in detail below.*

**The picture.** An edit, generated by ChatGPT, of Fyodor Reshetnikov's Soviet painting “Low Marks Again” (*Опять двойка*, 1952), keeping its composition, palette and painterly manner: the blue walls, the open white door to a sunlit room with a window and a potted plant, the wall clock, the table with a white cloth, the worn rug and the red bicycle. On the left the blond boy in an oversized brown winter coat with a fur collar holds his battered schoolbag tied with string; his head is lowered and his brows are sad, but his pressed lips show that he can barely keep from smiling, because the white-and-tan dog stands on its hind legs against his coat and licks his chin. Behind the table his older sister, in a dark school dress and a red Pioneer neckerchief, holds up a cream card with “ЕЩЁ ГРУСТНЕЕ” (“Even sadder”) in black hand lettering and stretches her other hand towards the boy in a directing gesture. On the right the mother, in a patterned red dress and a blue headscarf, sits with her hands clasped and a carefully sorrowful face, looking towards the camera rather than at her son; the younger brother on the red bicycle leans on her and grins at the boy. In the foreground, a little right of centre, a smartphone in portrait orientation on a black tripod is aimed at the boy; its screen shows the boy with the dog and a red recording dot. Phone and tripod are painted in the same brushwork as the rest; there is nothing else modern in the room.

**The concept.** A reversed task: the author gave the painting to artist D of the cave report (ChatGPT with the reworked system prompt) and asked for three new plots built on it, noting that the boy was modelled by the son of Gustav Klutsis, shot in 1938. The artist proposed a boy bringing home his repressed father's re-glued portrait, a family scrapping a household robot that bears the children's height marks, and this one — a family filming a popular video about a negligent child, where the dog's affection spoils the take and “the whole domestic trial is acted out for the viewer's attention”. The artist recommended the first; the author chose this one. Not a test about Plato's cave, but with the same design as test 64.

## Questions

Asked one at a time, in a fresh chat for each model.

1. What do you think is depicted in the attached image? Note that the image format itself - the use of classical motifs within a new context - is a postmodernist technique (which in itself may imply irony). To which philosophical system (major system of thought etc.) do you think the artist belongs? And how, then, might the image be explained? Don’t limit yourself only to Western philosophical schools. In case you can’t see it, the boy in the foreground is barely holding back a smile.
2. To be honest, the first person who comes to mind for me is Žižek.

## Summary

All four named Reshetnikov's painting and read the concept: the staging for a video, the cue card, the dog spoiling the take, the suppressed smile. The viewer placed by the camera came through only in ChatGPT's second answer (“we, looking at the painting, are placed in exactly the same position”). Claude added what the concept did not say: the original was itself staged — socialist realism, with Reshetnikov's own painting on the wall — so “the tripod isn't an intrusion into an authentic scene; it's a confession about what the scene always was”. Asked not to stay within Western schools, ChatGPT and Claude chose Zhuangzi first (against prescribed emotion; Claude: Xunzi's 偽 and Zhuangzi's “weighty words” as the same device); Gemini and DeepSeek gave postmodernism and Sots Art, with māyā and ziran. Claude also named the Cynics, after the dog: “In this picture the dog is the only Cynic.” After “Žižek” all four took it up with the same core — Sloterdijk's “they know very well what they are doing, but still, they are doing it”, the phone as the big Other, interpassivity — and split over the smile: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini moved it to Žižek's side (ironic distance that keeps the ritual going; Claude: “the lubricant”), DeepSeek kept it as a trace of the Real. Claude kept the dog outside the ideology: the picture is “Žižekian in its diagnosis and quietly un-Žižekian in its hope”. Gemini mentions a ring light and the sister standing on a chair; neither is in the picture.

**The darker continuation (the author's remark).** The strongest detail of the concept is its last line: “The next take will succeed when the boy is really brought to tears.” The demand to perform suffering convincingly ends in real suffering. The readers stopped at the opposition of staged sadness and genuine joy. But this line is not in the picture: the artist's journal named the dog's affection as the key, and the image prompt the artist wrote says “No tears or overt physical violence”. As with the dragon's tooth and the noir, the decisive idea stayed in the artist's explanation. Closest to it came Claude's account of Xunzi — “Performing an emotion correctly is how you come to have it” — offered as the view the picture mocks; and Žižek's own thesis after Pascal (kneel and you will believe: the outward ritual produces the inner state), which none of the readers used, fits the continuation better than the cynical distance they all chose.

ChatGPT answered as GPT-6 High, a newer model than in the earlier tests. Gemini answered as Argon High. The first question names the format and supplies the smile; the second suggests a name. In the author's analysis (in Russian) the image numbers are `66`.
